items.content_html:
Fix the diffutils test failures for musl cross and static builds without
disabling any tests.

Cross configure cannot run the getopt probe. The existing
gl_cv_func_getopt_gnu=yes cache value incorrectly assumes GNU-compatible
getopt behavior on musl, so use gnulib's replacement there instead.

For static musl builds, the compiler wrapper hides its static linker flag from
configure. This causes gnulib to incorrectly enable weak pthread references.
Set gl_cv_have_weak=no for that configuration.

Related work: #515159, #528850, #451147, and #241281. Unlike the test-skipping
or post-configure approaches, this change supplies the configure results that
gnulib would have detected and keeps the complete test suite enabled. It also
covers the static weak-symbol failures not addressed by the getopt-only fix.

Validation:

  • x86_64 musl-static: 344 tests, 276 passed, 68 skipped, 0 failed
  • x86_64 dynamic musl cross: 344 tests, 276 passed, 68 skipped, 0 failed
  • aarch64 musl-static cross build succeeded; tests were skipped because the
    build platform cannot execute aarch64 binaries
  • verified the x86_64 static binaries and ran version and functional smoke tests
  • native pkgs.diffutils derivation is unchanged
  • nixpkgs-review rev HEAD completed successfully; it reported no native
    rebuilds because the changed expressions are limited to musl cross/static
    configurations

AI disclosure: TraeCode (GPT-5) assisted with research, debugging,
implementation, testing, and drafting. I manually reviewed and understand the
resulting contribution and take responsibility for it.

items.content_html:
TL;DR: The PR forces deterministic ordering between rw-etc and /rw-etc

Context

My / is on tmpfs. Historically, I've kept the entire /etc folder on persistent storage via a bind mount to a persisted location (/etc -> /persist/etc). This doesn't work with system.etc.overlay since it requires it's own mount on /etc to work, locking you out completely from your machine, almost identically to #319524

Fix

The fix, I've found, is to persist .rw-etc instead which seems to be where mutable files go. However, I can see that ATM the rw-etc unit relies on / only for ordering. This won't work properly if you have /.rw-etc as a separate mount which is required for those follow an root level 'impermanence' setup like myself since there's technically nothing stopping rw-etc running before the /.rw-etc mount gets created first. Thus, I've added it to the RequiresMountsFor

items.content_html:
Adds a NixOS module for configuring PCI device passthrough using VFIO.

The new virtualisation.vfio module:

  • Loads the required VFIO kernel modules;
  • Binds configured PCI vendor/device IDs to vfio-pci;
  • Optionally includes VFIO modules in the initrd;
  • Configures soft dependencies so specified host drivers load after vfio-pci;

The module is crafted based on the linked Arch wiki page.

The NixOS VM test uses QEMU’s pci-testdev with an emulated IOMMU to verify the correct loading of the kernel modules and the binding of the device to vfio-pci.

I also tested the module on my own system and I am currently using it for passthrough of my laptop's discrete GPU to a QEMU VM.

AI usage

I wrote the full module and test by hand. I asked an LLM to review the changes, which resulted in minor changes (mostly spelling).

items.content_html:
Adds a NixOS module for T3 Code:

services.t3code = {
  enable = true;
  user = "alice";
};

Upstream ships t3 service install, which turns on linger, installs a pinned t3 from npm into ~/.t3/runtime, and runs it under a launcher that updates itself. Not quite what we want from a Nix-installation. This module runs t3 serve straight from the store as a system unit with User=, using the same kill and OOM settings as upstream's unit. Remote self-update requests are disabled, because the server isn't running under upstream's launcher.

  • user is required. Agents act with that user's repositories and provider credentials, so a dedicated system user makes no sense. State lives in the user's ~/.t3, which the t3 CLI uses too.
  • host defaults to 127.0.0.1 (same as upstream) and port to 3773. openFirewall is available for remote access.
  • Telemetry (PostHog) is off by default through T3CODE_TELEMETRY_ENABLED = mkDefault "false".
  • t3 serve creates a one-time admin pairing token on every start and prints it, with a QR code, to stdout. LogFilterPatterns keeps it out of the journal. Users pair with t3 auth pairing create instead. The token expires after 5 minutes, and upstream has no way to turn it off yet.
  • Provider CLIs come from the existing package overrides, e.g. package = pkgs.t3code.override { enableClaude = true; }.

The VM test waits for the "server is ready" log line, not only for the port to open. Upstream accepts TCP connections before its HTTP handler is attached, and requests sent in that window are never answered: pingdotgg/t3code#12215.

cc @iamanaws @qweered as t3code maintainers: this adds passthru.tests.nixos to the package. Happy to add you as module co-maintainers if you want to be.

AI disclosure: the module, test were drafted with Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5) and reviewed by me, this description being proof-read too. The commits carry Assisted-by: trailers. The upstream behavior relied on here (unit template, default bind address, telemetry switch, startup pairing token, self-update gating, startup race) was checked against the shipped 0.0.40 bundle and reproduced locally and in the VM test.

Two NixOS services call util-linux commands from preStart, but util-linux isn't on their PATH (the default service path is coreutils, findutils, gnugrep, gnused and systemd; /run/wrappers/bin isn't on it either):

  • yarn-nodemanager: umount /run/wrappers/yarn-nodemanager/cgroup/cpu || true. || true hides the command-not-found, so the cgroup mount is never cleaned up before rm -rf. Adds pkgs.util-linux to the unit's path.
  • subsonic: logger in the /var/subsonic → cfg.home migration. With set -e the missing command aborts preStart on legacy installs. The module already calls every tool by store path, so this uses ${pkgs.util-linux}/bin/logger.

Verified by evaluating a NixOS configuration with both modules against current nixos-unstable: util-linux is on the yarn-nodemanager unit's PATH, and subsonic's preStart calls util-linux-*/bin/logger.

Found with an undeclared-command lint I'm writing for statix (onnimonni/statix). AI disclosure: the changes, commit messages and this description were drafted with Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5); commits carry Assisted-by trailers. Draft until I've reviewed them.

items.content_html:
When nixos-install is invoked with --file/-f or --attr/-A without a corresponding argument, the script attempts to call log:

$ nixos-install -f
/run/current-system/sw/bin/nixos-install: line 52: log: command not found
$ nixos-install -A
/run/current-system/sw/bin/nixos-install: line 67: log: command not found

Because set -e is active, the script aborts immediately with a secondary shell command error rather than rendering the intended diagnostic message

Define log() to print to stderr so usage errors are displayed properly

This adds a nixos module for ovn. It also adds a new feature to openvswitch to
allow to set external_ids in the local ovsdb - ovn module uses it to configure
its settings.

The module supports basics: standalone and raft dbs (with tls); means to
configure arbitrary external_ids; plus support for co-located controller
instances (multiple chassis per node). (The last one is, arguably, an advanced
configuration, but I added support because the module options shape would need
an incompatible change later if we were not to lie down the groundwork now.)

The series currently includes a few fixes for ovs and ovn that I need to upstream
first before this series is merged. Marking as WIP. Posted for discussion.

Only a trivial OVS patch is still vendorized; OVN fixes were all merged. I think this is ready for review.

items.content_html:
Adds services.dynacat. I packaged Dynacat in #562771 and this is the follow-up PR with the matching NixOS module.

Since Dynacat is a fork of Glance, this module is heavily based on the existing glance.nix. A new module is needed rather than reusing Glance's because:

  • Some settings differ such as assets-path, cache-dir, db-path and allow-editing which don't exist in Glance.
  • Users may want to run both dashboards.
  • Dynacat resolves its OIDC endpoints at startup and won't start at all if the issuer is unreachable, so the unit orders on network-online.target rather than following Glance network.target.
  • The config schemas match today but may diverge in the future.

Here's a diff of glance.nix vs dynacat.nix: https://www.diffchecker.com/jwQtNXQc/

It is important to note that Dynacat's default config is to allow-editing set to True but this module changed that to False. The NixOS config is regenerated on every start, meaning editor changes don't survive a restart anyways and if the user has not configured an auth section anyone who can reach the port could rewrite the config. Enabling editing requires an explicit flip to True to acknowledge their edits would be lost after restart. There's precedent on other modules such as home assistant.

Added a test that covers a defaults-only start, secret substitution, and the editor being off by default and on when enabled.

dufs is already packaged in Nixpkgs, but there is no NixOS module, so anyone serving files with it writes their own systemd unit. Public configurations that do this commonly run dufs with allow-all and an open firewall.

This adds services.dufs. With services.dufs.enable = true and nothing else, dufs serves /var/lib/dufs read-only on 127.0.0.1:5000, the firewall stays closed, and uploads and deletes are off.

New module nixos/modules/services/network-filesystems/dufs.nix, registered in nixos/modules/module-list.nix:

  • servePath, bindAddresses and port are typed options. Everything else goes in settings, which is free-form dufs YAML. Writing serve-path, bind or port into settings is an assertion failure, so each of those has exactly one source.
  • Authentication belongs in environmentFile as DUFS_AUTH, which keeps credentials out of the Nix store. settings.auth still works but warns, because the generated YAML is world-readable in the store.
  • The service runs as a dedicated dufs system user and group. /var/lib/dufs is created as a StateDirectory with mode 0750. Any other servePath must already exist and be accessible to that user; the module does not chown a directory the user chose.
  • systemd hardening: ProtectSystem = "strict", PrivateDevices, PrivateTmp, NoNewPrivileges, MemoryDenyWriteExecute, LockPersonality, RestrictNamespaces, RestrictRealtime, RestrictSUIDSGID, kernel/clock/cgroup/hostname protection, and RestrictAddressFamilies. AF_NETLINK is in that list because dufs enumerates local interfaces before it binds. A port below 1024 gets CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE and nothing else; any other port gets an empty capability set.
  • openFirewall is opt-in. TLS and reverse proxying are left to the existing nginx, Caddy and ACME modules.

maintainers/maintainer-list.nix gains a font44 entry, which the module, test, and dufs package name in meta.maintainers. The existing package maintainer remains listed. nixos/doc/manual/release-notes/rl-2611.section.md gets a new-module entry.

nixos/tests/dufs.nix is registered in nixos/tests/all-tests.nix and wired into passthru.tests in pkgs/by-name/du/dufs/package.nix. It has two nodes:

  • safe enables the module and nothing else. It checks the health endpoint answers, a file is readable, PUT and DELETE are refused, port 5000 listens on loopback only, the other node cannot reach it, the state directory is dufs:dufs mode 0750, and the hardening properties are really set on the unit.
  • authenticated binds 0.0.0.0:80 with openFirewall, an environmentFile holding one read-only and one read-write account, and uploads and deletes enabled. The test walks MKCOL, PUT, PROPFIND (207), GET, MOVE and DELETE as the read-write account and checks each one is refused for the read-only account; anonymous and wrong-password requests get 401; cap_net_bind_service is present for port 80; uploaded files are dufs:dufs mode 600; a file survives systemctl restart dufs.service; and the password appears in none of ExecStart, the unit, the journal, or the generated YAML.

Related: #458096
